text: starting the demand model build this week. the deck says 70% commercial, 80% first pass -- should i use those for the base case and sensitivity around them?
no. thats not what the coverage matrix or the claims pull say — commercial ~55, blended first pass is high 50s not 80
okoro said the same thing at the ad board last tuesday, 'not the 80s the manufacturer decks always assume.' the transcript is in the interviews folder
high 50s blended feels low for a product this differentiated tbh. its the only maintenance option built for GPP

its not a vibes number, its the segment-level rates from the matrix weighted by the actual claims mix. medicaid sitting at 40 first pass drags the blend down no matter how differentiated the product is

Aaron -- the model uses the coverage matrix rates and the claims-extract weights. The deck figures can appear in an appendix labeled 'client planning assumption, not adopted.' Please label them exactly that way.
ok will do. appendix it is
also distribution, since aaron's draft still says open across 15 SPs -- thats a marketing slide, we picked four. the network options file has the selection flags, 4 of 12 candidates got a Y
wait when did that get decided?? i had 15 in my workflow draft from the deck

trade finalized the shortlist with the hub vendor last week. limited distribution -- cold chain, hub integration and data reporting were the filters. update your draft, the csv is the decision of record

And a reminder for the deliverables: distribution, pricing, and copay design are all 'recommended, pending Veloxa legal and pricing-committee sign-off.' We do not describe anything as final or approved before that gate.

one more from tanya's field note over the weekend -- a plan rep quoted her 15 business days for a standard PA determination. that wont fly in the statute states -- its 7 days / 72 hours in most of them, 10 in FL and MO, 14 in TN, all still way under 15 business days. the statutes csv has the citations by state

so the workflow SLAs get built to each state's statutory clock -- 7 calendar days standard / 72 hrs expedited in most statute states -- and anything a plan quotes beyond that is an escalation not an SLA?
exactly. the 15-day quote goes into the workflow as a compliance escalation trigger, not a design target. we hold plans to the statute

Good. And make the expedited lane explicit in the spec -- acute GPP presentations can't sit in a standard queue. The 72-hour pathway plus the step-therapy exception package is the spine of the clinical access story.
drafting the workflow steps tonight w/ the denial reason codes as failure paths. will circulate tomorrow am for markup
Thank you. Cite sources inline as you go -- retrofitting citations at the end is how errors survive.
